transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood), Samira Ortiz (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lin (Aegis SRE), Priya Kapoor (Aegis Head of Platform), Daniel Reeves (Aegis CTO), Sara Vance (Aegis Security)

Summary: quick follow-up to the outage on 2026-09-08. Walk through postmortem findings, mitigation timeline, and next steps for reliability improvements and SLA.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. we'll keep this tight. this is a postmortem follow-up from the outage on Thursday, uh the 8th. Samira will run through the technical findings then we'll discuss remediation, S L A and next steps.
[00:24] Samira: Thanks Jordan. quick recap: root cause was an autoscaler regression in our serving runtime that caused open connections to be dropped during a burst, which in turn invalidated some prefix KV cache entries. the combination led to increased cold starts and fallback to the larger model variant - causing latency spikes and request timeouts for a subset of streaming requests.
[00:47] Marcus: just to be clear, from our side we saw a spike in 5xxs at 03:40 UTC and roughly 30% of streaming requests timed out during peak. we also noticed a lot of reconnects from our API layer.
[01:05] Samira: yep that's consistent. one of the probes for the autoscaler mis-evaluated the GPU memory footprint during a multi-tenant burst - that triggered an aggressive scale-down. when pods restarted the KV cache invalidation wasn't properly sequenced which created a cold path.
[01:28] Priya: is this the same KV cache you mentioned in the original postmortem where you said 'key V cache' in one place, just want to confirm it's the prefix/kv cache in serving runtime.
[01:40] Samira: yes sorry, transcription oddities in the doc, it's the prefix KV cache used for hot sequences. sometimes the doc autofill showed K V cache, but it's the in-memory prefix cache.
[01:52] Daniel: the bigger concern for us is the failover to the larger model variant. that wasn't anticipated since we pin model versions per route. why did the routing policy pick a bigger model?
[02:05] Samira: routing has a fallback policy for capacity constraints. when Dedicated pool reported insufficient capacity the orchestrator routed to the next compatible variant which happened to be a higher-memory model on a different pool. our fallback threshold logic had an off-by-one that mis-classified temporary memory pressure as sustained.
[02:29] Jordan: I want to reiterate: we owned the bug. patch was deployed Friday morning, and we ran a controlled rollout and didn't see recurrence in our internal staging.
[02:42] Marcus: we did see a regression window during your roll-out where our telemetry showed brief increased latencies, but overall it's much improved.
[02:55] Samira: mitigation steps implemented: reverted the autoscaler probe to the previous stable probe, added a sequencing guard on KV cache invalidation so restarts don't flush live entries, and tightened fallback thresholds. we also added more conservative routing for cross-pool fallbacks.
[03:15] Priya: will those changes be in the hosted plane only or do they affect Dedicated customers? we run Dedicated reserved capacity.
[03:25] Samira: the fix is in the serving runtime and will be rolled out across Hosted and Dedicated - it's a runtime binary change and config. Dedicated pools will receive the patch in the next maintenance window; we've prioritized Aegis and two other large Dedicated customers.
[03:40] Sara: security question - did the incident surface any exfil or access to logs beyond what you normally provide? we need to know for compliance.
[03:50] Samira: no indicators of exfil. the logs we collected were standard audit logs and diag traces; we redacted customer payloads. we can provide an artifact list and the exact log entries we used - attached to the final postmortem.
[04:05] Daniel: on SLAs - we want to understand how Redwood will make us whole. explicit credit, timeline for credit, and a remediation bank so this doesn't recur.
[04:17] Jordan: absolutely. Liam from CSM will open the formal SLA credit request and coordinate with finance. we'll propose a credit based on the downtime and the contract. also propose additional reliability commitments: quarterly joint runbooks, a dedicated redwood SRE contact during high-risk rollouts, and a shared benchmark plan.
[04:39] Liam: I'll start the ticket after this call and cc finance and your procurement.
[04:46] Marcus: on benchmarks - we need to replay approx one week of peak traffic with prefix caching enabled to validate. do you have a replay harness we can run in our environment?
[04:58] Samira: yes we have a replay harness that can be run against a Dedicated pool or in your staging env. we'll provide a dockerized harness and a reference yaml. we've also prepared a benchmark spreadsheet that lists configurations, sequence lengths, and expected p99 latency.
[05:18] Priya: about rolling back config changes - can you guarantee we won't get evicted during maintenance? we have 99.9 latency sensitive customers.
[05:27] Samira: for Dedicated we'll schedule a maintenance window and can enable graceful draining and KV cache persistence to minimize impact. for critical windows we can do a canary on a subset of nodes first.
[05:39] Marcus: earlier in the thread you mentioned autoscaler probe changes - is that open source/visible in the repo or is it internal? we want to audit the change.
[05:48] Samira: the autoscaler is part of our internal runtime, but we can provide the diff and explanation and the test cases we ran. not open-source, but Redwood will provide the code snippet and the CI logs.
[06:00] Jordan: ok key points: patch deployed, fixes described, no exfil, Dedicated patch prioritized. next steps: postmortem doc + artifacts, run benchmark, SLA ticket.
[06:12] Daniel: can you also add a timeline of the incident with exact timestamps? our audit requires minute-level detail for the escalation.
[06:20] Samira: yes we'll add minute-level telemetry plus flamegraphs and the autoscaler logs.
[06:29] Jordan: also wanted to surface an idea - longer term reliability improvements: incremental checkpoints of KV cache to persistent fast storage to survive restarts; smarter routing that considers recent churn; and a rollout scheduler that respects customer high-traffic windows. thoughts?
[06:47] Priya: checkpointing sounds promising but we worry about added latency on writes. if it's async and only used during restart, might be ok.
[06:55] Samira: agree, async checkpointing with a TTL would be the approach. and we can gate it behind a config flag per-customer for Dedicated.
[07:04] Marcus: we'd prefer a per-tenant opt-in so we can test in staging first.
[07:09] Jordan: makes sense. we'll propose an opt-in beta for checkpointing and schedule a pilot with Aegis.
[07:17] Sara: compliance also wants to see where the audit logs live and retention policies. we need a doc.
[07:24] Liam: we'll attach the retention and KMS info to the postmortem pack.
[07:30] Samira: quick note on monitoring: we added two new alerts - cache-invalidation-rate and autoscaler flapping - and created dashboards for p50/p95/p99 per-route. we'll share links.
[07:44] Marcus: that will help. if we can get the dashboard URLs and be added to alerting, that would expedite root cause detection on our side.
[07:53] Samira: we'll add Aegis SRE to the alerting policy for the Dedicated pool.
[08:00] Jordan: ok let's go through the planned timeline and owners (recap).
[08:06] Jordan: Postmortem doc + artifacts (Jordan/Samira) - due 2026-09-16.
[08:12] Jordan: SLA credit ticket (Liam) - by 2026-09-17.
[08:15] Jordan: Deep-dive on autoscaler + KV cache (Samira + Marcus) - schedule by 2026-09-20.
[08:21] Jordan: Benchmark replay (Marcus) - results by 2026-09-23.
[08:27] Priya: on the bench results if we identify regressions we want an on-call hotfix path - is that something Redwood can commit to?
[08:36] Jordan: yes we'll have a hotfix path and a dedicated SRE for the pilot period.
[08:41] Daniel: one more ask - can you provide a short blameless postmortem summary we can share internally? high-level timeline, customer impact, fixes and mitigations.
[08:52] Jordan: yes we'll draft a blameless summary in bullet form as part of the pack.
[08:58] Marcus: anything else from the Redwood side?
[09:02] Samira: we'll include the patch diff, CI results, flamegraphs, and the replay harness.
[09:08] Liam: I'll open the SLA ticket after this and ping procurement.
[09:13] Sara: we'll send the compliance checklist for required logs.
[09:17] Jordan: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc and schedule.
[09:22] End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: medium - some product names in transcript may be mistranscribed (eg 'K V cache' vs 'KV cache', 'auto-scaller' vs 'autoscaler').

Recap / explicit next steps: 1) Redwood to send final postmortem + artifacts (2026-09-16). 2) Liam to open SLA credit ticket and coordinate credits (2026-09-17). 3) Samira and Marcus to schedule deep-dive and run benchmarks (2026-09-20 and 2026-09-23). 4) Redwood to enable Dedicated patch and opt-in checkpoint pilot for Aegis (TBD).
